problem: Pointing-only robot navigation must run costly pointing-gesture recognition continuously, and inaccurate user pointing directions can send the robot to the wrong place.
motivation: Pointing is a more natural way to specify targets than long verbal descriptions, but keypoint estimation is expensive and pointing is noisy. Short voice commands with demonstratives ("that", "there") can tell the robot whether pointing is needed at all and can disambiguate the target.
key_idea: Use voice as the primary channel: run pointing estimation only when the spoken command is insufficient, and snap the noisy pointing ray to the nearest object matching the spoken description.
insight: Most commands (e.g. 'go to that door' with a unique door, or 'go forward') do not need pointing, so skipping OpenPose-based estimation saves most of the processing time (T 151.73 ms to 30.61 ms). When several candidate objects exist, choosing the described object nearest the ground intersection point tolerates inaccurate pointing, and satisfaction scores rise versus pointing-only. The intersection-point error grows with distance (17.85 cm near, 82.26 cm far), which motivates the voice snapping.
method: Voice understanding: PocketSphinx STT after a wake-up word, then an LTP dependency parser (Chinese) mapped to structured instruction templates such as goto(chair, black, that).
Gesture gating: skip pointing estimation when the instruction has no demonstrative pronoun or the described target object is unique in the environment.
Pointing direction estimation: OpenPose 2D keypoints plus depth give 3D eye and wrist points; the eye-to-wrist vector (REW or LEW, chosen by arm angle to the body) is transformed into the map frame.

Target decision: if the command has an object description, take the ground intersection point P, build the candidate set of matching annotated objects, and choose the one with the smallest Euclidean distance to P. Otherwise the target is P itself.

Navigation: Cartographer 2D lidar SLAM and move_base path planning on a TurtleBot 2, with pre-annotated object positions and properties; TTS error prompts are issued when no person or no pointing gesture is detected.

setting.backbone: OpenPose (pretrained keypoints), PocketSphinx STT, LTP dependency parser, rule-based target decision
setting.training_data: none (uses off-the-shelf pretrained components, no training)
setting.observation: RGB-D camera (Asus Xtion Pro Live) plus 2D lidar (Sick TIM561), voice
setting.action_space: navigation goal position published to move_base (planned path, wheeled base)
setting.privileged: pre-built SLAM map and manually pre-annotated object positions and properties

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; only custom real-robot experiments (processing time, intersection offset, user satisfaction in a figure), so none are listed.
results: VGPN cuts total processing time from 151.73 ms to 30.61 ms (about 79.8%) when pointing is unnecessary, compared with the pointing-only approach. In the object-description experiments (SAME/DIFF), almost all volunteers were satisfied with VGPN's accuracy but not with pointing-only (scores only in a figure).
limitations: Small evaluation (5 volunteers), custom setup, and satisfaction scores shown only in a figure, with no comparison to other published methods.
Requires a pre-built map and manually annotated objects; only Chinese commands are supported; VGPN can still fail when the pointing is nearer to the wrong same-category object.
